target_customer: Custom manufacturing shops and plants with frontline workers
problem: Shops run on tribal knowledge held by veterans who are retiring, and workers cannot easily get answers or file issues without an app.
business_model: B2B software agent over SMS and messaging apps, pricing not public

founders.name: Justin So
founders.background_notes: YC page lists finance work at Arm. One article says his father runs a manufacturing facility, which prompted the product, from a secondary source.

founders.name: Aadip Khanal
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by RuntimeWire (https://runtimewire.com/article/sidekick-factory-operations-sms-ai-agent); the YC page lists only Justin So.

competitors.name: Swarf AI
competitors.what: CNC focused copilot for machine shops

competitors.name: Canvas Envision
competitors.what: Captures retiring workers' knowledge for training

competitors.name: OpsMate AI
competitors.what: Factory floor agents using site documents and logs

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrieval over shop documents, messaging integrations and work order routing use existing LLM tooling, though integrations with machine data add work.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated shop knowledge could create lock in, but several startups and large industrial software vendors offer similar assistants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent manufacturing software vendors were launching AI assistants, for example Syspro's platform. No sourced action against Sidekick.

market_need_then: Trade press in 2025 widely described a manufacturing knowledge gap as baby boomer machinists retire.

branding.name_origin: Name suggests a helper role, and the site says Every hero needs a Sidekick, but no source states the origin
branding.domain_note: Uses textsidekick.com with a text prefix, so sidekick.com was not used

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, positions the agent as a member of the team

branding.brand_signature: Every hero needs a Sidekick tagline

brand_strength.rationale: The metaphor fits the product, but Sidekick is a heavily reused name across software, with many unrelated products found, which hurts search.

outcome_analysis: Sidekick joined YC in Summer 2026 with a solo founder and has no exit or failure. A secondary profile reports 20 plants and 600 workers by July 2026, which is unverified. The no app SMS design lowers adoption friction in shops, while a generic name and many AI assistant rivals make differentiation and enterprise sales the main risks.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators show an undisclosed pre-seed, or $500K with conflicting batch and date, single aggregators only, so no round recorded. A Chinese language article names Aadip Khanal as a co-founder, but YC page lists only Justin So, so he is excluded. Traction of 20 plants and 600 workers comes from one profile site. Completeness pass: a 500K pre-seed is recorded from VCBacked alone with no date, because dates conflict (June 2026 VCBacked, January 2026 elsewhere) and one aggregator says 12M total, which looks unreliable. No press found. Aadip Khanal is added as co-founder on RuntimeWire's report; the YC page does not list him.
